findings.summary: The 'question' is the old title with 'Go ahead with this:' in front, so the card still leads with the same text the owner called unclear
findings.evidence: `question: format!("Go ahead with this: {}?", phrase(&item.title))`. Before this change the card's h3 was item.title, which is the problem statement the owner complained about. A title such as 'Verifier misses broken links' becomes 'Go ahead with this: Verifier misses broken links?', which is not a yes/no decision in plain words. Better: make the proposal state its decision (a question field, or a check that refuses a title that is not a decision), or at least check the title and say plainly when it cannot be phrased as a question.

findings.summary: The 'If yes' and 'If no' lines are the same fixed text on every card, so they say nothing about the decision
findings.evidence: yes_line is always 'If yes: Athena makes this change and works with it from then on.' and no_line is always 'If no: nothing changes. Athena keeps working as it does today.' They use nothing from the proposal: not its title, rung or evidence. The request asks for one line on what happens if yes and one on what happens if no for each decision. Identical lines leave the owner where they started. The reading's assumption says the lines are derived from the title and rung; these are not.

findings.summary: 'Recommend no' is given for every proposal above the raising role's limit, which turns 'you must decide this' into invented advice against it
findings.evidence: `Some(_) => "Recommend no: it is bigger than Athena may change on its own, so it needs your care."`, and None (role not recorded) is also 'Recommend no'. The old text said 'Decide yourself'. That a change is above the role's limit says who must decide, not whether the change is good. The reason given ('needs your care') does not support 'no'. Once the filter in job 20261103-201526-t4qv lands, the page shows only above-limit proposals, so every card would say 'Recommend no' with the same reason. This breaks the owner-style rule 'nothing invented'. Better: recommend from something in the record, or state plainly that Athena makes no recommendation on the merits.

findings.summary: The jargon ban is tested only on hand-picked titles; jargon in a real title (role names, 'job', rung names) reaches the visible question unchecked
findings.evidence: The sample title was changed from the request's example '...every job?' to '...every task?' so the test's own ban list would pass. Brief::check enforces the word count and the recommendation line, but not the jargon rule. The 'mechanism' default asks that the rule be enforced in the renderer, not only in fixtures. The CHANGELOG line 'the visible text no longer names rungs or roles' therefore overclaims.

findings.summary: A 'Recommend yes' card says the change is small enough for Athena to make on its own, which makes it unclear why it is on the owner's page
findings.evidence: 'Recommend yes: it is small enough for Athena to change on its own.'

findings.summary: The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met
findings.evidence: The reading says the yes/no, cost and risk text is 'derived by code from the title, rung and the raising role's recorded limit, with plain-word templates'. The candidate meets the letter of that but not the request. The 'If yes' and 'If no' lines are fixed text that is the same on every card. The question is the old title with a prefix. The request's goal, that the owner can tell what they are deciding in five seconds, depends on per-decision content that the records do not hold. The reading should have raised that gap, for example as a needed question or outcome field, or as a check on titles, instead of assuming templates would be enough.

summary: Verdict: fail. All seven criteria are met: I ran the decisions tests in `cargo test -p xtask` and all 11 pass, Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed, and the diff stays within the deliverables list. But three major soundness problems mean the owner still cannot tell what they are deciding. First, the 'question' is the old problem-statement title with 'Go ahead with this:' in front. Second, the 'If yes' and 'If no' lines are the same fixed text on every card. Third, every proposal above the raising role's limit gets 'Recommend no' with the same reason. That is invented advice, and once the filter in job 20261103-201526-t4qv lands, every card on the page would say it. Also, the jargon ban is checked only on hand-picked titles: the test changed the request's own example from 'job' to 'task' so its ban list would pass. The tests check that the layout is right, not that the content tells the owner anything.
